source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Simple and Compound Propositions under 2.4, as printed (PDF 27, printed 23).

blocks.text: A simple proposition contains only one statement. It cannot be broken into smaller parts. For example, “It is raining” is a simple proposition. A compound proposition is formed by combining two or more simple propositions. Logical connectives are used to join them. For example, “It is raining and it is cold” is a compound proposition. Compound propositions can express complex ideas. They are common in logical reasoning. Both types are important in propositional logic.
